block.comment: Read the block header and its body. block.md#detection: On the line of the header, a statement may follow the header after whitespace, and a `;` or `%%` after it is a node, not a separator or a comment. common.md#leading-whitespace: Whitespace, line terminators, directives, and comment regions before the first unit of the diagram's lexer are trivia and are not seen by the diagram's grammar.

patterns.comment: Columns, whitespace, and digits, or columns, whitespace, and auto: a columns unit with the number or auto. A directive between two complete components is allowed. block.md#the-statement-context: `columns`, whitespace, and digits: a `columns` unit with the number, and `columns`, whitespace, and `auto`: a `columns` unit with `auto`. block.md#directives-inside-units: A directive between two units, also glued to them, is allowed: `A%%{init: {}}%%` followed by `:2`, `-->B`, or a line feed, `space:` followed by it and `2`, and one between the string of a shape or a block arrow and its opening or closing.

Space: and digits, and space not followed by a word character: a space unit. block.md#the-statement-context: `columns`, whitespace, and digits: a `columns` unit with the number, and `columns`, whitespace, and `auto`: a `columns` unit with `auto`.

After classDef and whitespace, the class definition context reads one or more ASCII word characters as class-id, whitespace, then the rest of the line as styles. A common comment after a line separator or paragraph separator ends this value before the separator. The required whitespace after the class-id is checked without consuming it, so a separator before a common comment remains outside the begin. block.md#classes-and-styles: The styles are the parts between `,` of the rest of the line without the whitespace at its ends; the class name of `class` is the rest of the line as one text, which may be empty and may hold whitespace, so `class A c d` gives the class `c d`. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

AccDescr, whitespace, {, whitespace and } is an empty description block where a statement starts; a block with text is rejected. Retain this local form: rejects a block with text and permits an empty block after a node; it is not the common accessibility statement. A common comment after a line separator or paragraph separator ends this value before the separator. block.md#empty-description-blocks: An **empty description block** is a statement where a statement starts: on the line of the header, between two statements, before the first, and inside a composite, with whitespace inside it or a line feed, as in `A accDescr {} B`. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

<[ enters the block arrow context, which reads a string, then ]>, whitespace and (, then one or more directions and ). A direction is right, left, up, down, x or y; comma and whitespace may precede a direction. A common comment after a line separator or paragraph separator ends this value before the separator. block.md#block-arrows: A direction is `right`, `left`, `up`, `down`, `x`, or `y`, in lower case; a `,` and whitespace may stand before a direction, line feeds included, and two directions need nothing between them: `(right down)`, `(right, down)`, and `(rightdown)` are the directions `right` and `down`. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

An opening arrow is --, == or -. after optional <; its label is a string followed by an arrow. block.md#edges: The arrow may have another line than the opening arrow: `A -- "x" ==> B` is accepted.
